evidence: internal/cli/audit_schema.go:21 renders '- evidence_file: repo-relative path when status is PASS or PARTIAL; null for FAIL'. A probe (fresh git repo, /tmp/tp-dev/tp audit spec.md --affected-files app/a.go --json) shows that line in the security and maintainability-conventions prompts. Corpus, both globs, canonical audit-round-N.ndjson: 33 of 39 file_check FAIL rows carry no evidence_file. Of 432 non-PASS slug-scheme file_check rows with an evidence_file, 24 cite a file other than the item's subject, e.g. 0.36.0 audit-round-12 item file-maintainability-conventions-github-workflows-ci-yml-… PARTIAL error, evidence_file internal/cli/quality_gate_config_test.go. HEAD's prior-round path lists a row with no evidence_file under its id (internal/cli/audit.go:574-587; TestAuditPriorRound asserts the 'prior-nofile' FAIL row is listed, audit_prior_round_test.go:77).
finding: Decision 1b, written by the repair, keys a prior file_check row on evidence_file and says a row without one 'answers none'. But the audit prompt tp emits tells every role to write evidence_file null for FAIL, so a FAIL row that follows the schema answers no item. The prior-round section would then drop every such prior FAIL. That is the row §2 Context says must reach the role under the right id, and HEAD does list it (under a correct id whenever no suffix collision re-pointed it). The rule also applies to rounds recorded after this release, where the recorded id is stable and correct, so d1b gives up a correct key for good. Separately, evidence_file is not always the item's subject: some PARTIAL rows cite a supporting file, and d1b re-keys them onto that other file's item. That brings back the across-rounds defect §2 closes: a prior verdict listed under an id the checklist attaches to a different file. Rows 2 and 4d can only be built with a FAIL row that breaks the schema.
suggestion: Match a prior file_check row by its recorded id when the round was recorded under this release's derivation, and fall back to evidence_file only for rounds recorded before it. A schema-conformant FAIL then keeps its item. Alternatively, change the audit schema so a file_check FAIL names its file and say so in §2.1. Either way, give row 2 and row 4d a schema-conformant FAIL fixture.

evidence: Spec lines 50-55 (decision 1), 73-74 ('A residual collision ... decision 2 refuses the pair'), 92 ('Decision 1 removes the known cause'), 185-188 (rows 1-3). internal/cli/audit_roles.go:98-121 and 129-149: the id is the 40-char slug plus the seen-counter suffix. finding: Decision 1 no longer requires different paths to get different ids. The round-1 repair withdrew the uniqueness clause, yet §6 row 3 asserts 'four distinct ids' for four files in one deep directory. HEAD's cut slug with the suffix removed is a function of role and cleaned path alone, keeps a readable prefix and has no positional suffix, so it meets every clause of decision 1. It passes row 1, because every file's id is identical in both emissions: all of them share one. It fails row 3 only through a requirement no decision states. Under it every deep directory is a 'residual collision', so decision 2 refuses every hand-sharded round, and §2.2's 'Decision 1 removes the known cause' is false for a conforming build. Rows 1-3's mutants also name a counter that never fires once ids are unique ('restore the positional suffix', 'restart the suffix per emission'), so read literally they change nothing.
suggestion: Add to decision 1: two different cleaned repo-relative paths get different ids, except by a collision of a digest taken over the whole cleaned path (the digest and its length stay the task's). Derive row 3 from that clause, and rename the mutants of rows 1-3 to 'derive the id as HEAD does: the cut slug plus a positional suffix'.

evidence: internal/cli/audit_schema.go:13-21 renderAuditOutputSchema, 'embedded in every audit prompt': 'evidence_file: repo-relative path when status is PASS or PARTIAL; null for FAIL'. finding: Decision 1b makes a prior file_check row answer an item only through its evidence_file, and 'a row without an evidence_file answers none'. The output schema tp embeds in every audit prompt requires the opposite for the one status the prior-round section exists to carry: 'evidence_file: repo-relative path when status is PASS or PARTIAL; null for FAIL'. So a schema-compliant FAIL on a file_check item answers no item in the next round, even one recorded by the new binary under exactly the id the current checklist gives that file, because 1b ignores the recorded id for file_check rows 'whatever id it was recorded under'. That is a regression for the non-colliding case: at HEAD such a FAIL is listed under its recorded id and reaches the right item. §2 Context's motivating failure is a prior FAIL, and rows 2 and 4 only pass because their fixture's FAIL carries an evidence_file the schema tells the grader to leave null (the sidecar's Run A row does). suggestion: Choose one and say it in §2.1. (a) Make the schema require, for a file_check item, a field naming the item's own file whatever the status (evidence_file or a new subject field), and read that field in d1b and d2. (b) Let a row without that field answer the item whose decision-1 id equals its recorded id, and say how a decision-1 id is told apart from an older slug id. Then make row 2's FAIL schema-compliant (evidence_file null) and replace row 4b's mutant.

finding: The repair made evidence_file the only field that tells a file_check collision apart ('name different files in evidence_file'), and §2.1's consequence relies on it: 'a residual collision … is not silent: decision 2 refuses the pair wherever it meets'. In the other direction, the repair's own reasoning for exempting spec-derived items ('evidence_file is the grader's citation rather than the item's subject') holds for some file_check rows too. Two overlapping shards that agree on a PARTIAL for one file but cite different supporting files are refused, and the hint's remedy, re-grading, does not converge on a citation choice.

evidence: The spec text is §2.2 d2 ('conflict when they carry different verdicts — status, severity, or a disposition's status'), where only the evidence_file clause is limited to file_check. Row 5d covers only an agreeing status. In review-round-1.ndjson, the architect's §2 high finding says '(and often its status: a shard that lacks the implementing file reports PARTIAL)' and its resolution evidence reads 'd2 compares evidence_file only for file_check items; row 5d'. At internal/cli/audit.go:777 the truncation notice says 'name the rest with --affected-files'. spec-coverage's file list is taken from the audited set, which is each shard's own --affected-files (sidecar #32b: 'spec-coverage's selection keeps only task-mapped files', with a fallback to the named files).
finding: For spec-derived items decision 2 still compares status and severity. In a hand-sharded round run with the default panel, each shard's spec-coverage grades the same list-/table-/task- ids against a different file list, so a shard that lacks the implementing file returns PARTIAL or FAIL where the shard holding it returns PASS. That disagreement is built into sharding; it is not a defect in the rows. --merge exits 1 and --record refuses. The refusal's hint prescribes re-grading, which cannot settle the pair: re-grading in either shard hands the grader the same partial file list, so the same verdict comes back. The only way to exit 0 is to delete a verdict, which is the choice §2.2's 'Why' says tp is not entitled to make silently and which the hint forbids. So Non-Goal 3's 'makes a hand-sharded round merge honestly' holds only for shards emitted with --role and no spec-coverage. The truncation notice the spec cites as the workaround ('name the rest with --affected-files') does not say --role. Round 1's architect finding named this status half. The repair (8dafa6ed) scoped only evidence_file, and row 5d pins a pair whose status agrees.
suggestion: Decide what a spec-derived item graded in several shards is. One option: spec-coverage is emitted in one shard only, and the truncation notice names --role for the code roles in the others. Another: disagreeing spec-derived verdicts across --merge inputs are settled by a stated rule (the worse verdict stands, and the pair is reported in the payload) rather than refused. Then add a §6 row: two default-panel shards whose spec-coverage rows disagree on one task item's status.

finding: Decision 1b's 'Why by file' treats a file_check row's evidence_file as 'the file the grader read', and so as the item's subject. §2.2 says of spec-derived items that evidence_file is 'the grader's citation rather than the item's subject', and tp's own corpus shows the same holds for file_check rows. When a code file contradicts a doc, the grader cites the doc. Decision 1b re-files every such prior row under the cited file's item, or, when that file is not on this round's list, lists it as answering no item. Either way the role spends its re-check on the wrong item, or reads a prompt row that feeds no decision, while the item the row actually graded gets no prior context. The recorded id, which 1b discards 'whatever id it was recorded under', is right for these rows. It becomes fully trustworthy for every round recorded after this release, because decision 1 removes the one thing that corrupted it. evidence: Read §2.2 decision 2 bullets 1–3 and Why, and §2.1 Consequences bullet 3 ('decision 2 refuses the pair wherever it meets'). Read the sidecar 'Built before review', bullet on the withdrawn uniqueness clause ('refused a pair of which neither row is wrong, with no way through but dropping a verdict'). Read internal/engine/briefcommand.go:68-89: recordBriefCommand renders `[ -f %s ] || tp %s --merge … -o %s%stp %s %s --record %s` with separator '; ' for the audit phase. skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:189-202 confirms the merge step is guarded by the merged file's absence on retry, and gives the unit-failure stop at REFERENCE.md:235.
finding: The --record hint pinned in decision 2 ('a checklist item takes one row … a pair is settled by re-grading the item, not by deleting either row') gives the agent no action it can carry out, for three reasons. (1) Every settlement of a conflicting pair ends with a file holding at most one row for that (role, item_id). That means removing or rewriting a row, which the hint's second clause forbids. (2) For a residual collision — two files decision 1 maps to one id, which §2.1's last consequence sends to decision 2 — re-grading gives back the same two correct rows. The pair can never be settled. The sidecar's 'Built before review' already recorded this as 'no way through but dropping a verdict', and the round-1 repair brought the case back when it withdrew the uniqueness clause. (3) The hint does not say which file takes the settled row. --merge names pairs 'by input and line' (the role files), and --record names them by line in the merge output. Under tp run the audit-record brief is `[ -f $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson ] || tp audit --merge … -o merged.ndjson; tp audit <spec> --record merged.ndjson`, and decision 2 keeps --merge writing -o on the conflict exit. So a retry skips the merge, and a settlement written into the role files, where --merge pointed, never reaches the retried record. Each retry fails the same way until unit-failure.
suggestion: Pin the hint as an action and a place: 're-grade the item and replace the pair with one row in <the file named>'. Make --record's pair locations the ones to edit, since that file is the one a retried chain reads. For a pair whose two rows name different files under one id, have the refusal say it is an id collision a re-grade cannot settle, and state in §2.1 what the operator does about it. Alternatively, have decision 1 bound the digest so that a collision within one merged round is not expected, and say so instead of routing it to decision 2.

evidence: internal/engine/briefcommand.go:68-89: recordBriefCommand renders '[ -f %s ] || tp %s --merge $TP_ROUND_DIR/role-*.ndjson -o %s; tp %s %s --record %s' for audit. Lines 59-64 say the guard exists so that a retried record unit does not merge over dispositions. Spec §2.2 Decision 2: '--merge … still writes -o, holding both rows of each pair'; the --record hint: 'a pair is settled by re-grading the item, not by deleting either row'. The §2.2 Why: 'ends in --record's refusal naming the pair, not in a missing file'.
finding: The repair made --merge write -o, holding both rows, on the conflict exit, so that the ';'-chained audit record unit reaches --record's refusal rather than a missing file. That part works. But the record unit's merge is guarded by the merged file's absence ('[ -f $TP_ROUND_DIR/merged.ndjson ] || tp audit --merge …'). Once the conflict exit has written merged.ndjson, every retry of the unit skips the merge and re-runs --record against the same conflicting file. The remedy decision 2's hint names, 're-grading the item, not … deleting either row', rewrites a role-*.ndjson that no retry ever merges again. Under tp run a conflict therefore ends in the same refusal on every attempt and then unit-failure. The only moves that change the outcome are deleting merged.ndjson or deleting a row from it. The spec does not name the first, and the hint forbids the second, which is the silent choice between two verdicts that decision 2 exists to take away from an unattended unit. A re-grade reproduces two files under one id, and the only way through is to drop a verdict. The sidecar measured this dead end before review round 1 ('refused a pair of which neither row is wrong, with no way through but dropping a verdict'). Withdrawing the uniqueness clause brought it back without a remedy.
suggestion: Make the collision impossible by construction rather than rare: say decision 1's id is injective over cleaned repo-relative paths, which the implementing task meets by length or encoding. Or have an emission that would hand one id to two of its files exit non-zero naming both (the id stays a function of the path). Or have the refusal's hint distinguish 'two files, one id' from 'one item, two verdicts'.

finding: 'its shell test runs in the project gate' changes the repository's gate without saying how, and the two ways to do it land in different tasks with different blast radii. No *-test.sh runs in the gate today, and no Go test execs one. One way is a fifth `&&` step in .tp/config.json. That fails TestCIRunsEveryStepOfTheProjectGate and the resolved-gate literal in quality_gate_config_test.go until .github/workflows/ci.yml and that literal change, it makes CLAUDE.md's four-step gate text false, and it needs python3 on CI. The other way is a Go test that execs the script inside step 1's `go test -count=1 -race` wrapper. The task that closes 'its shell test runs in the project gate' cannot be sized until one is chosen.
suggestion: Name the mechanism in the consequence, for example 'a Go test runs scripts/audit-round-prep-test.sh and fails on its non-zero exit', or move gate composition out of this spec. evidence: Spec §2.1 d1b: 'a round without an id_scheme marker is not comparable, both as today'. Spec §2.1 Why: 'every round recorded before this release usable at once, with no marker to trust'. Spec §6 row 4c's mutant: 'match a marker-less round's rows by file too'.
finding: 'Matching on it makes every round recorded before this release usable at once, with no marker to trust' contradicts decision 1b's last sentence two paragraphs earlier, which keeps 'a round without an id_scheme marker is not comparable, both as today', and row 4c pins that. Marker-less rounds are recorded before this release and are not usable. The argument the Why gives, that evidence_file makes the marker unnecessary, would apply equally to their file_check rows, so the text neither says why they stay excluded nor limits the quantifier.
suggestion: Narrow the Why to 'every round carrying an id_scheme marker', and say in one clause why a marker-less round's file_check rows are not matched by file (its spec-derived ids are positional), or drop the exclusion for file_check rows.

evidence: internal/cli/audit_schema.go:17-26 (the row fields; no 'type'). internal/cli/audit.go:49: type is a ChecklistItem field, emitted in the prompt only. internal/cli/audit_roles.go:93-121: file_check ids are 'file-'+roleID+'-'+slug. finding: The repair made both decision 1b and decision 2 depend on whether a row answers a file_check item or a spec-derived one: prior rows are matched by file or by id, and evidence_file is compared or not. A recorded or merged row does not carry its item's type. The emitted schema has item_id, status, evidence_file, evidence_lines, category, severity, notes and class, and no type. So --merge, --record and the prior-round section have to infer the type, either from the id's 'file-<role>-' prefix or from the role not being spec-coverage. The two readings disagree on the case decision 2's Why names first, 'a role that misnames an id'. A code role's row under an id without the prefix is a file_check row by role, so its evidence_file is compared, and a spec-derived row by prefix, so it is not. The same pair is refused under one implementation and merged under the other.
suggestion: State the test, for example 'a row is a file_check row when its role is not spec-coverage', and add it to row 5d's fixture as the contrasting case.

evidence: Spec lines 84-90. Rows 5-7b all use exactly two rows per key.

evidence: Read §4 decision 3 ('Its payload carries recorded_round: false and matching_rounds … otherwise the payload says in words that the file is not a recorded round and that no round state changed'). Read internal/cli/audit_resolve.go:149-156: the stderr line is written with fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, …), and output.JSON carries only resolved_count, skipped_count, status, file, next_step. §6 rows 12, 12c and 12d assert 'the no-state-changed statement' in the payload. Sidecar #29: the report's 75 --resolve calls.
finding: After the round-1 repair keyed the actionable datum, decision 3 carries each fact twice. The payload holds `recorded_round: false` and `matching_rounds`, and it also 'says in words that the file is not a recorded round and that no round state changed'. The sentence adds nothing an agent can use: 'not a recorded round' is the boolean, and 'no round state changed' follows from it, since a write into a file no round state lists cannot change round state. tp already puts the human-readable side of this command on stderr — `resolved %d audit rows as %s (%d already resolved, skipped)` — and returns only keys in the JSON payload. The decision does not say which channel the words use or whether --compact strips them. Read as written, they ride in the JSON on every resolve into a non-recorded file outside a run. The field report's own flow made 75 such calls, one per row.
suggestion: Have decision 3 put the statement on stderr, beside the existing 'resolved N audit rows' line, and keep the JSON payload to `recorded_round` and `matching_rounds`. Carry `matching_rounds` only when `recorded_round` is false, so that on a resolve into the recorded round file it does not repeat `file`. Rows 12, 12c, 12d, 12g and 13 then assert the statement on stderr.

evidence: internal/engine/childenv.go:22 and :43: TP_ROUND is the oracle's round as an int. internal/cli/audit_resolve.go:246-247: next_step is 'tp audit <spec> --record %s' with the spec left as a placeholder. Spec §4 Decision 2 and Decision 3 ('every spec whose round state lives in the repository holding the file'). The sidecar's 'Ground round 1' documents the stale-TP_ROUND rewrite.
finding: The repair rewrote decision 2's condition as TP_ROUND 'names one of the recorded rounds the file's rows match (decision 3)'. It also widened decision 3's search to 'every spec whose round state lives in the repository'. TP_ROUND is a bare round number, and matching_rounds lists round files across specs. As written, TP_ROUND=N is satisfied by another spec's round N whose rows happen to contain the file's. Such rows exist: round-1 finding 'Decision 3 names … as if there is only ever one' gives identical rows in two specs auditing the same files, and a file with no content rows is contained in every round. The step that is then offered, 'tp audit <spec> --record <file>', runs under the unit's own spec. A TP_ROUND that is stale for that spec reaches the rewrite-an-earlier-round or append outcome that ground round 1 measured and row 10b exists to prevent, through a round of a different spec.
suggestion: Bind decision 2's match to the spec whose round state holds the run's task file (TP_FILE): the step is offered only when matching_rounds contains that spec's round TP_ROUND.

evidence: Spec §6 preamble, line 178. Row 4d 'from' column: '§2.1 *prep*'. Spec §2.1 Consequences, second bullet. Round-1 tester row (class untested-consequence) had noted that §6 admits only rows derived from numbered decisions. The repair added row 4d without changing the preamble.
finding: §6's preamble says 'Every row derives from a numbered decision', but row 4d derives from '§2.1 *prep*', a Consequences bullet (scripts/audit-round-prep.py's re-measure listing), and no numbered decision states that behaviour. Rows 8-9c cite §3's single unnumbered 'Decision'. Either the preamble's rule, which tells a reader that each row is traceable to a decision, is false for four rows, or the prep-script change is a decision the spec has not written as one.
suggestion: Either promote the prep-script behaviour to a numbered decision in §2.1 (and number §3's decision), or reword the preamble to 'Every row derives from a decision or a stated consequence'.

evidence: Measured at HEAD. A FAIL row already carrying "resolved":{"status":"wontfix","resolved_at":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","evidence":"old"}, run through `tp audit f.ndjson --resolve-all fixed ...`, was skipped (skipped_count 1) and came back as {"item_id":"x-2","resolved":{"evidence":"old","resolved_at":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z","status":"wontfix"},...}. The value is equal, and a byte comparison of the line is False. Spec line 219.
finding: --resolve-all rewrites every row of the file with sorted keys, including the rows it skips. Row 14b's 'byte-identical' therefore fails a correct implementation on any fixture whose resolved block is not already in sorted-key order, and passes on one that is.
suggestion: Assert that the PASS row's resolved block is value-equal, or require the fixture to be one that tp wrote.
